To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
patients included in randomized clinical trials on knee cartilage repair are not representative of the general population of cartilage patients.

1) the heterogeneity of the general cartilage population and the variation in the inclusion criteria in the randomized controlled trials (RTCs) may question whether RCTS actually represent the general knee cartilage population; 2) the present study suggests that the results from published RCTS may not be representative for the general cartilage patient population.

The heterogeneity and the variation in the inclusion criteria in the randomized controlled trials (published RCTs) may question whether the results from the published RCT are representative for the general population of cartilage patients.

the fact that RCTs may be biased and that the results of the trials may not be applicable to all the general cartilage population.

the question of whether patients included in RCTs are representative of the general cartilage population.
